The code is AGPL-3.0: use it, run it, read it, fork it, sell a service built on it — and if you run a
**modified** version as a network service, publish your changes. That is deliberate. Improvements come
back to everyone instead of being resold as a closed product.

⚠️ One person maintains this. Reviews and replies may take time; that is the honest trade for a codebase
this size. A clear, reproducible report is worth more than a large speculative pull request.

---

## Where things go

| You have | Put it in |
|---|---|
| A question, or "how do I…" | [**Discussions**](https://github.com/FifeCIC/Trading-Command-Suite/discussions) → Q&A |
| An idea, or a "should it…" | **Discussions** → Ideas |
| A reproducible defect | **Issues** — with the command, the output and what you expected |
| A fix | A pull request, small and scoped |

## What a useful defect report contains

The project's whole culture is *evidence over assertion*, and it applies to reports as much as to code.

- **The command or click path**, verbatim.
- **What you saw** — the actual output or number, not a summary of it.
- **What you expected**, and why.
- **Whether it is active or merely possible.** "The UI lets me pick an option the backend ignores" is
  reachable; "25 of 26 records are configured to use it" is active. The second is a different priority
  and a different fix.

Numbers make a report fixable: *"the score was 71, the threshold was 75, and it still dispatched"* is a
bug report. *"It behaves oddly"* is not.

## Before you change code

```powershell
npm run build                       # frontend: fast, always safe
npm --prefix nest run typecheck     # backend types, no Prisma generate
npm --prefix nest run build:api     # backend: stop → build → restart → health
```

⚠️ Never `npm --prefix nest run build` while the API is up — it fails with an `EPERM` naming a temp
file and never mentions the running process. Use `build:api`.

⚠️ Never `prisma db push`. See [Troubleshooting](Troubleshooting).

## Conventions that will surprise you

| Convention | Why it exists |
|---|---|
| **Comment blocks are long and explain *why*** | The reasoning is deliberately at the code site — the next person editing that file will not open an issue |
| **Numbers in documentation are generated** | A number typed into prose is a second copy, and the second copy rots. If you need a count, it belongs in `docs/GENERATED-FACTS.md` |
| **"Cannot judge" is preferred to a confident answer** | An empty list and a failed query must never render the same |
| **Guards ship with a self-test that can fail** | A check that has never been observed to fail is decoration. `--self-test` on any validator should prove it can refuse |
| **Changing a scoring weight or threshold needs a copied configuration** | Live maths is compared side by side, not edited in place — otherwise there is nothing to measure against |
| **State what you did *not* do** | A partial change reported as complete is the one thing worse than a partial change |

## Areas that need help

The open issues are the honest list. The ones that would change the project most:

- **Packaging** — an installer or container so the app can be run without a developer ([#1147](https://github.com/FifeCIC/Trading-Command-Suite/issues/1147))
- **Live-account safety** — the real-account gate and risk acknowledgement ([#1153](https://github.com/FifeCIC/Trading-Command-Suite/issues/1153))
- **Data coverage** — more providers verified, more symbols with a confirmed route
- **Documentation** — a step that confused you is a documentation bug, and you are the only person who
  can still see it
